content: Agrimonia eupatoria, commonly known as common agrimony, church steeples, or sticklewort, is a species of agrimony. The entire plant is characterized by a dark green color and is covered with numerous soft hairs. These soft hairs facilitate the attachment of the plant's seed pods to animals or humans that come into contact with it. The flower spikes of the plant emit a spicy aroma reminiscent of apricots. In folklore, Agrimonia eupatoria has been attributed with both medicinal and magical properties since the time of Pliny the Elder. According to Nicholas Culpeper, the plant is astrologically associated with the zodiac sign Cancer. Traditional beliefs held that it could heal musket wounds and protect against witchcraft. In the realm of herbal medicine, Agrimonia eupatoria was traditionally recommended as a remedy for insomnia and was often incorporated into herbal pillows for this purpose. It was also believed to have the ability to draw out splinters. Modern herbalists prescribe it for conditions affecting the kidneys, liver, and bladder. The plant is known to possess diuretic and expectorant properties and is sometimes used to address mild skin conditions such as acne. However, not all of these applications are supported by scientific evidence.
